This establishes soundness of 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t), including the leaf case, where only the width alternatives apply.

We next check that latching preserves this guarantee. Suppose 𝖣𝗈𝗇𝖾s​(v,k,t)=1\mathsf{Done}_{s}(v,k,t)=1, and let t0≤tt_{0}\leq t be the first round at which the flag changed from 00 to 11. If it was set by a bottom-up certificate evaluation, during either a scale search or a post-update sweep, then 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t0)\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t_{0}) held by the update rule. Otherwise it was set by the first branch of Resolve​(v,s,k)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k). In this case, the flag was still zero before the assignment, so the branch condition 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t0)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t_{0}) could only hold through 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t0)\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t_{0}). Hence either way, 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t0)\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t_{0}) holds.

The certificate argument above applies at the earlier round t0t_{0}, so vv was (s,k)(s,k)-safe at round t0t_{0}. If s=Ls=L, Lemma B.2 gives Lv​(t)≥Lv​(t0)L_{v}(t)\geq L_{v}(t_{0}), and therefore

V∗​(v)−Lv​(t)≤V∗​(v)−Lv​(t0)≤ρk/2.V^{*}(v)-L_{v}(t)\leq V^{*}(v)-L_{v}(t_{0})\leq\rho_{k}/2.

If s=Us=U, then Uv​(t)≤Uv​(t0)U_{v}(t)\leq U_{v}(t_{0}), and thus

Uv​(t)−V∗​(v)≤Uv​(t0)−V∗​(v)≤ρk/2.U_{v}(t)-V^{*}(v)\leq U_{v}(t_{0})-V^{*}(v)\leq\rho_{k}/2.

Thus a latched side remains safe. Since 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t) is the disjunction of 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t) and 𝖣𝗈𝗇𝖾s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Done}_{s}(v,k,t), the lemma follows. □\Box

We next verify that an unresolved parent always leaves a child obligation at a scale no finer than its own. This ensures that the recursive selection rule is defined.

Lemma B.4 (Capped recursive progress).

Fix a round tt, a finite scale k≥0k\geq 0, an expanded internal node vv, and a side s∈{L,U}s\in\{L,U\}. If ¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t), then the current scale-kk recursive rule has at least one finite capped child obligation whenever recursive work is attempted, i.e.,

  • •

    if (v,s)(v,s) is a selector case, then there exists u∈As​(v,k,t)u\in A_{s}(v,k,t) such that

    ¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(u,k,t)andKs≤k​(u,t)<+∞;\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(u,k,t)\qquad\text{and}\qquad K_{s}^{\leq k}(u,t)<+\infty;
  • •

    if (v,s)(v,s) is a comparison case, then As​(v,k,t)≠∅A_{s}(v,k,t)\neq\varnothing; for b=bs​(v,k,t)b=b_{s}(v,k,t),

    Ks¯≤k​(b,t)<+∞orKs≤k​(b,t)<+∞.K_{\bar{s}}^{\leq k}(b,t)<+\infty\qquad\text{or}\qquad K_{s}^{\leq k}(b,t)<+\infty.

Thus, when the budget permits, both the comparison and selector recursive branches have an admissible capped child whenever the parent side predicate 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t) is false.

Proof. We show that failure of the parent certificate leaves an unresolved child within the permitted range of scales. Since 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s\mathsf{Comp}_{s} includes 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s\mathsf{Cert}_{s}, ¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t) implies ¬𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t)\neg\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t).

Suppose first that (v,s)(v,s) is a selector case. If every child u∈As​(v,k,t)u\in A_{s}(v,k,t) satisfied 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(u,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(u,k,t), then the recursive selector alternative in the definition of 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t) would hold, contradicting ¬𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t)\neg\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t). Thus there is a child u∈As​(v,k,t)u\in A_{s}(v,k,t) with ¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(u,k,t)\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(u,k,t). Since the capped set defining Ks≤k​(u,t)K_{s}^{\leq k}(u,t) contains the index kk, this implies

Ks≤k​(u,t)<+∞.K_{s}^{\leq k}(u,t)<+\infty.

Now suppose (v,s)(v,s) is a comparison case. We first check that the active set is nonempty. If As​(v,k,t)=∅A_{s}(v,k,t)=\varnothing, then every child is discharged at scale kk: in the Max, LL, case every child uu satisfies

Uu​(t)≤λL​(v,t)+ρk/2or𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉L​(u,k,t),U_{u}(t)\leq\lambda_{L}(v,t)+\rho_{k}/2\qquad\text{or}\qquad\mathsf{Comp}_{L}(u,k,t),

and in the Min, UU, case every child uu satisfies

Lu​(t)≥λU​(v,t)−ρk/2or𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉U​(u,k,t).L_{u}(t)\geq\lambda_{U}(v,t)-\rho_{k}/2\qquad\text{or}\qquad\mathsf{Comp}_{U}(u,k,t).

These are the recursive discharge conditions for 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t), contradicting ¬𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(v,k,t)\neg\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(v,k,t). Hence As​(v,k,t)≠∅A_{s}(v,k,t)\neq\varnothing.

Let b=bs​(v,k,t)b=b_{s}(v,k,t) be the selected blocker. Its membership b∈As​(v,k,t)b\in A_{s}(v,k,t) gives

¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(b,k,t).\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(b,k,t).

Thus the set defining Ks≤k​(b,t)K_{s}^{\leq k}(b,t) contains kk, and consequently

Ks≤k​(b,t)<+∞.K_{s}^{\leq k}(b,t)<+\infty.

If Ks¯≤k​(b,t)<+∞K_{\bar{s}}^{\leq k}(b,t)<+\infty, the algorithm refines that exclusion side. If Ks¯≤k​(b,t)=+∞K_{\bar{s}}^{\leq k}(b,t)=+\infty, the finite same-side obligation is available instead. In either case, the comparison rule has an admissible child while 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t) is false. □\Box

The latching rule also prevents an obligation from incurring work after it has been certified.

Lemma B.5 (No same-scale rework).

Fix a finite scale kk, an explored non-root node vv, and a side s∈{L,U}s\in\{L,U\}. If Resolve​(v,s,k)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k) begins at round tt with 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t), then it sets 𝖣𝗈𝗇𝖾s​(v,k)←1\mathsf{Done}_{s}(v,k)\leftarrow 1 and returns (0,𝖼𝖾𝗋𝗍)(0,\mathsf{cert}) before issuing any oracle query, expanding any node, making any child call, or increasing any work counter. Consequently, once 𝖣𝗈𝗇𝖾s​(v,k)=1\mathsf{Done}_{s}(v,k)=1, the node remains (s,k)(s,k)-safe on ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}, and every later invocation of Resolve​(v,s,k)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k) returns zero before doing positive work.

Proof. After initializing any unused scale-local storage, Resolve​(v,s,k)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k) first tests 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t). If this predicate holds, the procedure latches 𝖣𝗈𝗇𝖾s​(v,k)\mathsf{Done}_{s}(v,k) and immediately returns (0,𝖼𝖾𝗋𝗍)(0,\mathsf{cert}). The procedure reaches every oracle query, expansion, child call, and counter increment only after this guard fails.

Each flag 𝖣𝗈𝗇𝖾s​(v,k)\mathsf{Done}_{s}(v,k) is initialized to 00 and can change only from 00 to 11. Once latched, 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t′)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t^{\prime}) holds at every later round t′t^{\prime} by definition. Lemma B.3 then gives (s,k)(s,k)-safety on ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta} at every such t′t^{\prime}. The initial guard at round t′t^{\prime} therefore returns before any positive work, regardless of subsequent changes to the comparison endpoint, blocker, or active set. □\Box

We next convert the first unresolved scale into an endpoint-error bound. The capped form applies to recursive child selection.

Lemma B.6 (Endpoint control at capped scales).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}. Fix a finite parent cap κ\kappa, a round tt, an explored non-root node xx, and a side s∈{L,U}s\in\{L,U\}. If

j=Ks≤κ​(x,t)<+∞,j=K_{s}^{\leq\kappa}(x,t)<+\infty,

then

{V∗​(x)−Lx​(t)≤ρj,s=L,Ux​(t)−V∗​(x)≤ρj,s=U.\begin{cases}V^{*}(x)-L_{x}(t)\leq\rho_{j},&s=L,\\[3.0pt] U_{x}(t)-V^{*}(x)\leq\rho_{j},&s=U.\end{cases}

If Ks≤κ​(x,t)=+∞K_{s}^{\leq\kappa}(x,t)=+\infty, then 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(x,κ,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(x,\kappa,t) holds, and therefore

{V∗​(x)−Lx​(t)≤ρκ/2,s=L,Ux​(t)−V∗​(x)≤ρκ/2,s=U.\begin{cases}V^{*}(x)-L_{x}(t)\leq\rho_{\kappa}/2,&s=L,\\[3.0pt] U_{x}(t)-V^{*}(x)\leq\rho_{\kappa}/2,&s=U.\end{cases}

Proof. If Ks≤κ​(x,t)=+∞K_{s}^{\leq\kappa}(x,t)=+\infty, the capped set contains no unresolved scale: every index 0≤i≤κ0\leq i\leq\kappa is complete on side ss, in particular i=κi=\kappa. Lemma B.3, applied at the cap, proves the bound.

Now let j=Ks≤κ​(x,t)<+∞j=K_{s}^{\leq\kappa}(x,t)<+\infty. If Ux​(t)=Lx​(t)U_{x}(t)=L_{x}(t), interval validity gives zero error. Otherwise, let ℓ=k¯​(x,t)\ell=\underline{k}(x,t). We first show j≥ℓj\geq\ell, which places the selected scale within the range controlled by the current width. If j<ℓj<\ell, then the dyadic definition of ℓ\ell gives

Ux​(t)−Lx​(t)≤ρℓ≤ρj/2,U_{x}(t)-L_{x}(t)\leq\rho_{\ell}\leq\rho_{j}/2,

using ρi+1=ρi/2\rho_{i+1}=\rho_{i}/2. The width alternative in 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍s​(x,j,t)\mathsf{Cert}_{s}(x,j,t) would hold, contradicting the defining property ¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(x,j,t)\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(x,j,t) of jj.

If j=ℓj=\ell, the width itself controls either endpoint error, since

Ux​(t)−Lx​(t)≤ρℓ=ρj.U_{x}(t)-L_{x}(t)\leq\rho_{\ell}=\rho_{j}.

If j>ℓj>\ell, then j−1≥0j-1\geq 0. Also j≤κj\leq\kappa, because jj belongs to the capped set, so j−1≤κj-1\leq\kappa. The minimality of jj therefore gives 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(x,j−1,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(x,j-1,t). Lemma B.3 bounds the endpoint error by

ρj−1/2=ρj.\rho_{j-1}/2=\rho_{j}.

These two cases prove the finite-jj claim for either side. □\Box

We can now bound the value gap across a selected edge. The argument uses only the current selection rule, so it also covers a child call blocked by its inherited budget.

Lemma B.7 (One-step localization under capped descent).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}. Fix a round tt, an expanded internal node vv, a side ss, and a finite scale kk such that ¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t). Let (u,su,ku)(u,s_{u},k_{u}) be the output of ChildObligation​(v,s,k)\textsc{ChildObligation}(v,s,k) evaluated at this state. Then ku<+∞k_{u}<+\infty, ku≤kk_{u}\leq k, and

|V∗​(u)−V∗​(v)|≤ρku.|V^{*}(u)-V^{*}(v)|\leq\rho_{k_{u}}.

Proof. We relate the child’s value gap to the endpoint that caused its selection. Lemma B.4 first ensures that the selected obligation is finite. The rule uses the capped scale ku=Ksu≤k​(u,t)k_{u}=K_{s_{u}}^{\leq k}(u,t), whether or not the available budget permits an actual call. Thus ku≤kk_{u}\leq k; the dyadic relation ρi+1=ρi/2\rho_{i+1}=\rho_{i}/2 then gives ρk≤ρku\rho_{k}\leq\rho_{k_{u}}. Write ρ¯=ρk\bar{\rho}=\rho_{k} and ρ=ρku\rho=\rho_{k_{u}}.

Selector cases. If vv is a Min node and s=Ls=L, then u∈arg⁡minx​Lx​(t)u\in\arg\min_{x}L_{x}(t). Let ww be a child attaining V∗​(v)=minx⁡V∗​(x)V^{*}(v)=\min_{x}V^{*}(x). The selected lower endpoint is accurate by Lemma B.6:

V∗​(u)−Lu​(t)≤ρ.V^{*}(u)-L_{u}(t)\leq\rho.

The selector ordering gives Lu​(t)≤Lw​(t)≤V∗​(w)=V∗​(v)L_{u}(t)\leq L_{w}(t)\leq V^{*}(w)=V^{*}(v). Together with V∗​(u)≥V∗​(v)V^{*}(u)\geq V^{*}(v), this places the value gap inside the endpoint error:

|V∗​(u)−V∗​(v)|=V∗​(u)−V∗​(v)≤V∗​(u)−Lu​(t)≤ρ.|V^{*}(u)-V^{*}(v)|=V^{*}(u)-V^{*}(v)\leq V^{*}(u)-L_{u}(t)\leq\rho.

For the Max, s=Us=U, selector case, the same argument uses the upper endpoints. Now u∈arg⁡maxx​Ux​(t)u\in\arg\max_{x}U_{x}(t), so a child ww attaining V∗​(v)=maxx⁡V∗​(x)V^{*}(v)=\max_{x}V^{*}(x) satisfies

Uu​(t)≥Uw​(t)≥V∗​(w)=V∗​(v).U_{u}(t)\geq U_{w}(t)\geq V^{*}(w)=V^{*}(v).

Lemma B.6 gives Uu​(t)−V∗​(u)≤ρU_{u}(t)-V^{*}(u)\leq\rho, and since V∗​(u)≤V∗​(v)V^{*}(u)\leq V^{*}(v),

|V∗​(u)−V∗​(v)|=V∗​(v)−V∗​(u)≤Uu​(t)−V∗​(u)≤ρ.|V^{*}(u)-V^{*}(v)|=V^{*}(v)-V^{*}(u)\leq U_{u}(t)-V^{*}(u)\leq\rho.

Comparison at a Max node. Suppose vv is Max and s=Ls=L. Since 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉L​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{L}(v,k,t) is false, Lemma B.4 gives AL​(v,k,t)≠∅A_{L}(v,k,t)\neq\varnothing. Let λ=λL​(v,t)\lambda=\lambda_{L}(v,t) and b=bL​(v,k,t)b=b_{L}(v,k,t), so the selected child is u=bu=b. We first establish V∗​(v)≤Ub​(t)V^{*}(v)\leq U_{b}(t) by bounding every child value. For a child xx with x∈AL​(v,k,t)x\in A_{L}(v,k,t), the definition of bb gives

V∗​(x)≤Ux​(t)≤Ub​(t).V^{*}(x)\leq U_{x}(t)\leq U_{b}(t).

If x∉AL​(v,k,t)x\notin A_{L}(v,k,t), then either

Ux​(t)≤λ+ρ¯/2,U_{x}(t)\leq\lambda+\bar{\rho}/2,

or 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉L​(x,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{L}(x,k,t). In the latter case, Lemma B.3 gives

V∗​(x)≤Lx​(t)+ρ¯/2≤λ+ρ¯/2.V^{*}(x)\leq L_{x}(t)+\bar{\rho}/2\leq\lambda+\bar{\rho}/2.

Membership b∈AL​(v,k,t)b\in A_{L}(v,k,t) gives Ub​(t)>λ+ρ¯/2U_{b}(t)>\lambda+\bar{\rho}/2. The bounds for active and inactive children are therefore both at most Ub​(t)U_{b}(t), proving V∗​(v)≤Ub​(t)V^{*}(v)\leq U_{b}(t). Since vv is Max, we also have V∗​(b)≤V∗​(v)V^{*}(b)\leq V^{*}(v). It remains to control the blocker’s upper-endpoint error.

When the selected side is UU at bb, Lemma B.6 gives

Ub​(t)−V∗​(b)≤ρ,U_{b}(t)-V^{*}(b)\leq\rho,

and the value ordering just proved yields

|V∗​(b)−V∗​(v)|=V∗​(v)−V∗​(b)≤Ub​(t)−V∗​(b)≤ρ.|V^{*}(b)-V^{*}(v)|=V^{*}(v)-V^{*}(b)\leq U_{b}(t)-V^{*}(b)\leq\rho.

If the rule instead selects side LL at bb, the opposite side has no unresolved capped scale:

KU≤k​(b,t)=+∞.K_{U}^{\leq k}(b,t)=+\infty.

Lemma B.6 therefore gives

Ub​(t)−V∗​(b)≤ρ¯/2≤ρ,U_{b}(t)-V^{*}(b)\leq\bar{\rho}/2\leq\rho,

which, substituted into the preceding gap inequality, again gives |V∗​(b)−V∗​(v)|≤ρ|V^{*}(b)-V^{*}(v)|\leq\rho.

Comparison at a Min node. For vv Min and s=Us=U, we bound every child value from below by the blocker’s lower endpoint. Lemma B.4 gives AU​(v,k,t)≠∅A_{U}(v,k,t)\neq\varnothing. Let λ=λU​(v,t)\lambda=\lambda_{U}(v,t) and b=bU​(v,k,t)b=b_{U}(v,k,t). An active child x∈AU​(v,k,t)x\in A_{U}(v,k,t) satisfies, by the definition of bb,

V∗​(x)≥Lx​(t)≥Lb​(t).V^{*}(x)\geq L_{x}(t)\geq L_{b}(t).

For x∉AU​(v,k,t)x\notin A_{U}(v,k,t), either

Lx​(t)≥λ−ρ¯/2,L_{x}(t)\geq\lambda-\bar{\rho}/2,

or 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉U​(x,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{U}(x,k,t), in which case

V∗​(x)≥Ux​(t)−ρ¯/2≥λ−ρ¯/2V^{*}(x)\geq U_{x}(t)-\bar{\rho}/2\geq\lambda-\bar{\rho}/2

by Lemma B.3. Since b∈AU​(v,k,t)b\in A_{U}(v,k,t), we have

Lb​(t)<λ−ρ¯/2.L_{b}(t)<\lambda-\bar{\rho}/2.

The active and inactive child bounds are therefore both at least Lb​(t)L_{b}(t), which proves V∗​(v)≥Lb​(t)V^{*}(v)\geq L_{b}(t). Since vv is Min, we also have V∗​(b)≥V∗​(v)V^{*}(b)\geq V^{*}(v). We now control the blocker’s lower-endpoint error.

When the selected side is LL at bb, Lemma B.6 gives

V∗​(b)−Lb​(t)≤ρ,V^{*}(b)-L_{b}(t)\leq\rho,

and the value ordering above yields

|V∗​(b)−V∗​(v)|=V∗​(b)−V∗​(v)≤V∗​(b)−Lb​(t)≤ρ.|V^{*}(b)-V^{*}(v)|=V^{*}(b)-V^{*}(v)\leq V^{*}(b)-L_{b}(t)\leq\rho.

If the rule instead selects side UU at bb, the opposite side is complete throughout the capped range:

KL≤k​(b,t)=+∞,K_{L}^{\leq k}(b,t)=+\infty,

and Lemma B.6 gives

V∗​(b)−Lb​(t)≤ρ¯/2≤ρ.V^{*}(b)-L_{b}(t)\leq\bar{\rho}/2\leq\rho.

Substitution into the gap inequality gives |V∗​(b)−V∗​(v)|≤ρ|V^{*}(b)-V^{*}(v)|\leq\rho, completing the comparison case. □\Box

At the root, scale selection has no parent cap. The same endpoint argument applies to the uncapped active scale.

Lemma B.8 (Endpoint control at node-local active scales).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}. Fix a round tt, an explored non-root node xx, and a side s∈{L,U}s\in\{L,U\}. If

k=Ks​(x,t)<+∞,k=K_{s}(x,t)<+\infty,

then

{V∗​(x)−Lx​(t)≤ρk,s=L,Ux​(t)−V∗​(x)≤ρk,s=U.\begin{cases}V^{*}(x)-L_{x}(t)\leq\rho_{k},&s=L,\\[3.0pt] U_{x}(t)-V^{*}(x)\leq\rho_{k},&s=U.\end{cases}

If Ks​(x,t)=+∞K_{s}(x,t)=+\infty, then the corresponding one-sided error is zero.

Proof. If Ks​(x,t)=+∞K_{s}(x,t)=+\infty because Ux​(t)=Lx​(t)U_{x}(t)=L_{x}(t), both errors are zero by interval validity. We may therefore assume positive width and write ℓ=k¯​(x,t)\ell=\underline{k}(x,t).

For k=Ks​(x,t)<+∞k=K_{s}(x,t)<+\infty, the definition gives k≥ℓk\geq\ell. If k=ℓk=\ell, the width bound defining ℓ\ell is

Ux​(t)−Lx​(t)≤ρℓ=ρk,U_{x}(t)-L_{x}(t)\leq\rho_{\ell}=\rho_{k},

which controls either endpoint error by interval validity. If k>ℓk>\ell, the minimality of kk in the definition of Ks​(x,t)K_{s}(x,t) gives 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(x,k−1,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(x,k-1,t). Certificate soundness at this preceding scale bounds the required error by

ρk−1/2=ρk.\rho_{k-1}/2=\rho_{k}.

Finally, suppose Ks​(x,t)=+∞K_{s}(x,t)=+\infty while the width is positive. Then 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(x,i,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(x,i,t) holds at every i≥ℓi\geq\ell. Lemma B.3 bounds the same endpoint error by ρi/2\rho_{i}/2 for all i≥ℓi\geq\ell. Letting i→∞i\to\infty and using ρi↓0\rho_{i}\downarrow 0 proves that this error is zero. □\Box

The root rule compares the leader with a full contender. Its choice of the coarser unresolved scale controls the endpoint errors needed to bound the selected action’s effective gap.

Lemma B.9 (Root active-call localization).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta} and ε=0\varepsilon=0. Consider an outer-loop round tt, and let x∈Ch⁡(r)x\in\mathrm{Ch}(r) be the root child selected by Algorithm 1, with selected side ss and finite active scale k<+∞k<+\infty. Then

Δxeff≤2​ρk.\Delta_{x}^{\mathrm{eff}}\leq 2\rho_{k}.

Proof. We combine the endpoint bounds at the selected scale with the overlap that prevents root stopping. Let

a∈argmaxy∈Ch⁡(r)Ly​(t),b∈argmaxy∈Ch⁡(r)∖{a}Uy​(t)a\in\mathop{\rm argmax}_{y\in\mathrm{Ch}(r)}L_{y}(t),\qquad b\in\mathop{\rm argmax}_{y\in\mathrm{Ch}(r)\setminus\{a\}}U_{y}(t)

be the current leader and challenger. The failed stopping test and ε=0\varepsilon=0 give

La​(t)<Ub​(t).L_{a}(t)<U_{b}(t).

For any root child yy, Definition 2.4 gives

Δyeff=max⁡{Δ∗,V∗​(r,a∗)−V∗​(r,y)}.\Delta_{y}^{\mathrm{eff}}=\max\{\Delta_{*},\,V^{*}(r,a^{*})-V^{*}(r,y)\}.

Thus Δa∗eff=Δ∗\Delta_{a^{*}}^{\mathrm{eff}}=\Delta_{*}, while for every nonoptimal root child y≠a∗y\neq a^{*},

Δyeff=V∗​(r,a∗)−V∗​(r,y),\Delta_{y}^{\mathrm{eff}}=V^{*}(r,a^{*})-V^{*}(r,y),

because V∗​(r,a∗)−V∗​(r,y)≥Δ∗V^{*}(r,a^{*})-V^{*}(r,y)\geq\Delta_{*}.

The leader is selected. If the selected child is aa, then k=KL​(a,t)k=K_{L}(a,t), and Lemma B.8 gives

V∗​(r,a)−La​(t)≤ρk.V^{*}(r,a)-L_{a}(t)\leq\rho_{k}.

The root selection rule also controls both endpoints of the challenger. Its full-contender scale kbk_{b} is either +∞+\infty, in which case both KL​(b,t)K_{L}(b,t) and KU​(b,t)K_{U}(b,t) are +∞+\infty, or it is finite with ρkb≤ρk\rho_{k_{b}}\leq\rho_{k}. In the latter case, the contender-side definition gives, for each s′∈{L,U}s^{\prime}\in\{L,U\}, either Ks′​(b,t)=+∞K_{s^{\prime}}(b,t)=+\infty or ρKs′​(b,t)≤ρkb≤ρk\rho_{K_{s^{\prime}}(b,t)}\leq\rho_{k_{b}}\leq\rho_{k}. Lemma B.8 therefore yields

V∗​(r,b)−Lb​(t)≤ρk,Ub​(t)−V∗​(r,b)≤ρk.V^{*}(r,b)-L_{b}(t)\leq\rho_{k},\qquad U_{b}(t)-V^{*}(r,b)\leq\rho_{k}.

If a=a∗a=a^{*}, then Δaeff=Δ∗\Delta_{a}^{\mathrm{eff}}=\Delta_{*}. Since bb is a competitor, the failed stopping test and the endpoint bounds give

Δ∗≤V∗​(r,a)−V∗​(r,b)<(V∗​(r,a)−La​(t))+(Ub​(t)−V∗​(r,b))≤2​ρk.\Delta_{*}\leq V^{*}(r,a)-V^{*}(r,b)<\bigl(V^{*}(r,a)-L_{a}(t)\bigr)+\bigl(U_{b}(t)-V^{*}(r,b)\bigr)\leq 2\rho_{k}.

The leader ordering gives La​(t)≥Lb​(t)L_{a}(t)\geq L_{b}(t), while the challenger bounds give Lb​(t)≥V∗​(r,b)−ρkL_{b}(t)\geq V^{*}(r,b)-\rho_{k} and Ub​(t)≤V∗​(r,b)+ρkU_{b}(t)\leq V^{*}(r,b)+\rho_{k}. Combining these inequalities yields

Δaeff=V∗​(r,a∗)−V∗​(r,a)≤Ub​(t)−La​(t)≤Ub​(t)−Lb​(t)≤2​ρk.\Delta_{a}^{\mathrm{eff}}=V^{*}(r,a^{*})-V^{*}(r,a)\leq U_{b}(t)-L_{a}(t)\leq U_{b}(t)-L_{b}(t)\leq 2\rho_{k}.

The challenger is selected. Now suppose the selected child is bb, with finite full-contender scale kk. For each s′∈{L,U}s^{\prime}\in\{L,U\}, either Ks′​(b,t)=+∞K_{s^{\prime}}(b,t)=+\infty or ρKs′​(b,t)≤ρk\rho_{K_{s^{\prime}}(b,t)}\leq\rho_{k}, by the contender-side definition. V∗​(r,b)−Lb​(t)≤ρk,Ub​(t)−V∗​(r,b)≤ρk.V^{*}(r,b)-L_{b}(t)\leq\rho_{k},\qquad U_{b}(t)-V^{*}(r,b)\leq\rho_{k}.

For the leader aa, either KL​(a,t)=+∞K_{L}(a,t)=+\infty, in which case the lower error is zero, or the algorithm’s choice of the challenger implies ρKL​(a,t)≤ρk\rho_{K_{L}(a,t)}\leq\rho_{k}. Hence

V∗​(r,a)−La​(t)≤ρk.V^{*}(r,a)-L_{a}(t)\leq\rho_{k}.

If b=a∗b=a^{*}, then aa is a competitor. The leader ordering bounds their value gap by the challenger’s lower-endpoint error:

Δbeff=Δ∗≤V∗​(r,b)−V∗​(r,a)≤V∗​(r,b)−Lb​(t)≤ρk,\Delta_{b}^{\mathrm{eff}}=\Delta_{*}\leq V^{*}(r,b)-V^{*}(r,a)\leq V^{*}(r,b)-L_{b}(t)\leq\rho_{k},

where we used La​(t)≥Lb​(t)L_{a}(t)\geq L_{b}(t) and La​(t)≤V∗​(r,a)L_{a}(t)\leq V^{*}(r,a). If b≠a∗b\neq a^{*} and a=a∗a=a^{*}, then the failed stop test gives

Δbeff=V∗​(r,a)−V∗​(r,b)<(V∗​(r,a)−La​(t))+(Ub​(t)−V∗​(r,b))≤2​ρk.\Delta_{b}^{\mathrm{eff}}=V^{*}(r,a)-V^{*}(r,b)<\bigl(V^{*}(r,a)-L_{a}(t)\bigr)+\bigl(U_{b}(t)-V^{*}(r,b)\bigr)\leq 2\rho_{k}.

In the remaining case, b≠a∗b\neq a^{*} and a≠a∗a\neq a^{*}. Since a∗≠aa^{*}\neq a, the challenger choice bb gives

V∗​(r,a∗)≤Ua∗​(t)≤Ub​(t)≤V∗​(r,b)+ρk.V^{*}(r,a^{*})\leq U_{a^{*}}(t)\leq U_{b}(t)\leq V^{*}(r,b)+\rho_{k}.

Δbeff=V∗​(r,a∗)−V∗​(r,b)≤ρk.\Delta_{b}^{\mathrm{eff}}=V^{*}(r,a^{*})-V^{*}(r,b)\leq\rho_{k}.

This covers every choice of the selected root child. □\Box

The root bound and the one-step bound combine without a loss at each depth, because capped descent never decreases the target tolerance.

Proposition B.10 (Active-call localization with explicit depth bound).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta} and ε=0\varepsilon=0. Consider any invocation Resolve​(v,s,k)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k) with finite scale kk made by Algorithm 1 during an outer-loop iteration. (s0,k0),(s1,k1),…,(sm,km)=(s,k).(s_{0},k_{0}),(s_{1},k_{1}),\ldots,(s_{m},k_{m})=(s,k).

Let t0t_{0} be the outer-loop round at which x0x_{0} was selected. For i≥1i\geq 1, let tit_{i} be the round, within the same nested execution, at which the call Resolve​(xi−1,si−1,ki−1)\textsc{Resolve}(x_{i-1},s_{i-1},k_{i-1}) calls Resolve​(xi,si,ki)\textsc{Resolve}(x_{i},s_{i},k_{i}). At round t0t_{0}, Lemma B.9 gives

Δx0eff≤2​ρk0.\Delta_{x_{0}}^{\mathrm{eff}}\leq 2\rho_{k_{0}}.

For each i≥1i\geq 1, apply Lemma B.7 at round tit_{i} to the call from xi−1x_{i-1} to xix_{i}. This gives

ki≤ki−1and|V∗​(xi)−V∗​(xi−1)|≤ρki.k_{i}\leq k_{i-1}\qquad\text{and}\qquad|V^{*}(x_{i})-V^{*}(x_{i-1})|\leq\rho_{k_{i}}.

Lemma B.11 (Local scale completion).

Lemma B.12 (Budgeted recursive spending).

Fix any execution of Algorithm 1. For every invocation Resolve​(v,s,k,B)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k,B), if the invocation returns (q,z)(q,z), then

0≤q≤B0\leq q\leq B

with the convention that the inequality is void when B=+∞B=+\infty. Moreover, if z=𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽z=\mathsf{blocked}, then q=0q=0. Finally, for every explored non-root node vv, scale kk, and round tt,

Mv,kexp​(t)≤𝖡v,krec=αh⁡(v)​Γv(k)​(δv).M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}(t)\leq\mathsf{B}_{v,k}^{\mathrm{rec}}=\alpha_{h(v)}\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v}).

Here an undefined scale-local counter is interpreted as zero.

Proof. We first show that every return respects the input cap and that a blocked call incurs no cost, by induction on the remaining depth h⁡(v)h(v). The certificate branch returns (0,𝖼𝖾𝗋𝗍)(0,\mathsf{cert}). In the local branch, LocalStep​(v,k,B)\textsc{LocalStep}(v,k,B) returns (0,𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽)(0,\mathsf{blocked}) if B<cB<c; otherwise it takes one slow sample and returns (c,𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗀𝗋𝖾𝗌𝗌)(c,\mathsf{progress}), with B≥cB\geq c. Thus both properties hold for the local branch: its cost is at most BB, and it spends nothing when blocked. This also proves the leaf case.

For an internal node, let

R=𝖡v,krec−Mv,kexp.R=\mathsf{B}_{v,k}^{\mathrm{rec}}-M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}.

If R≤0R\leq 0, the call uses the local branch just considered. Otherwise, its child-work cap is Brec=min⁡{B,R}B_{\mathrm{rec}}=\min\{B,R\}. For an unexpanded vv, the comparison with the expansion cost determines what happens. If |Ch⁡(v)|>R|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|>R, expansion exceeds the node’s own budget, so the call uses the local branch. If |Ch⁡(v)|≤R|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|\leq R but |Ch⁡(v)|>B|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|>B, expansion fits that budget but exceeds the inherited cap, and the call returns (0,𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽)(0,\mathsf{blocked}). In the remaining case,

|Ch⁡(v)|≤Brec≤B,|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|\leq B_{\mathrm{rec}}\leq B,

so expansion respects the cap.

If vv is already expanded, there is at most one child call, with cap BrecB_{\mathrm{rec}}. The induction hypothesis bounds its returned cost qq by Brec≤BB_{\mathrm{rec}}\leq B, and makes that cost zero if the child reports 𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽\mathsf{blocked}. When this happens and the inherited cap is binding (B<R)(B<R), the parent also returns (0,𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽)(0,\mathsf{blocked}). Otherwise it uses the local branch, which respects the cap and costs zero exactly when blocked. If the child is not blocked, the parent simply returns the child’s result. This completes the induction on the return properties.

It remains to bound Mv,kexpM_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}. This counter starts at zero, with undefined counters also read as zero, and has only two possible updates. When vv is expanded at scale kk, the algorithm first checks

|Ch⁡(v)|≤Brec≤R=𝖡v,krec−Mv,kexp,|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|\leq B_{\mathrm{rec}}\leq R=\mathsf{B}_{v,k}^{\mathrm{rec}}-M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}},

so adding the expansion cost leaves Mv,kexpM_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}} at most 𝖡v,krec\mathsf{B}_{v,k}^{\mathrm{rec}}. When a child call returns (q,z)(q,z) with z≠𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽z\neq\mathsf{blocked}, the parent adds to Mv,kexpM_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}} the cost qq. The return property just proved gives

q≤Brec≤R=𝖡v,krec−Mv,kexp,q\leq B_{\mathrm{rec}}\leq R=\mathsf{B}_{v,k}^{\mathrm{rec}}-M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}},

so this update also leaves the counter at most 𝖡v,krec\mathsf{B}_{v,k}^{\mathrm{rec}}. Since no other operation increases Mv,kexpM_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}, the bound holds throughout the execution. □\Box

Lemma B.13 (Aggregate obligation accounting).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}. Fix an explored non-root node vv and scale kk. Undefined scale-local counters are interpreted as zero. For every round tt,

Mv,kloc​(t)≤Γv(k)​(δv),Mv,kexp​(t)≤αh⁡(v)​Γv(k)​(δv).M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{loc}}(t)\leq\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v}),\qquad M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}(t)\leq\alpha_{h(v)}\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v}).

Mv,kloc​(t)+Mv,kexp​(t)≤(1+αh⁡(v))​Γv(k)​(δv).M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{loc}}(t)+M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}(t)\leq\bigl(1+\alpha_{h(v)}\bigr)\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v}).

Moreover, once Mv,kloc​(t)M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{loc}}(t) reaches Γv(k)​(δv)\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v}), both side predicates 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉L(v,k,⋅)\mathsf{Comp}_{L}(v,k,\cdot) and 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉U(v,k,⋅)\mathsf{Comp}_{U}(v,k,\cdot) remain true thereafter, and every later invocation of Resolve(v,s,k,⋅)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k,\cdot) for either side returns before doing positive work.

Proof. Lemma B.12 gives the recursive bound. For the local bound, we show that completion prevents the counter from passing its prescribed limit. The counter starts at zero, and only LocalStep​(v,k,B)\textsc{LocalStep}(v,k,B) increases it, by exactly cc each time. If Γv(k)​(δv)=0\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v})=0, Lemma B.11 gives both side certificates before any slow query at vv at scale kk. Thus Resolve(v,s,k,⋅)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k,\cdot) returns at its first branch and Mv,klocM_{v,k}^{\mathrm{loc}} stays zero.

If Γv(k)​(δv)>0\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v})>0, the identity Γv(k)​(δv)=Γv​(ρk,δv)\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v})=\Gamma_{v}(\rho_{k},\delta_{v}) shows that the limit is c​mv​(ρk,δv)c\,m_{v}(\rho_{k},\delta_{v}). Thus Mv,klocM_{v,k}^{\mathrm{loc}} cannot skip the limit: its values lie in {0,c,2​c,…,Γv(k)​(δv)}\{0,c,2c,\ldots,\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v})\} until completion. Upon first reaching Γv(k)​(δv)\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v}), Lemma B.11 gives

𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍L(v,k,⋅)and𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍U(v,k,⋅).\mathsf{Cert}_{L}(v,k,\cdot)\qquad\text{and}\qquad\mathsf{Cert}_{U}(v,k,\cdot).

The ensuing RefreshAndLatch​(k)\textsc{RefreshAndLatch}(k) in Algorithm 3 sets both 𝖣𝗈𝗇𝖾\mathsf{Done} flags. Therefore 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉L(v,k,⋅)\mathsf{Comp}_{L}(v,k,\cdot) and 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉U(v,k,⋅)\mathsf{Comp}_{U}(v,k,\cdot) remain true. By Lemma B.5, every subsequent call at this node and scale returns without positive work, on either side. The local counter therefore stays at most Γv(k)​(δv)\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v}).

Adding the two counter bounds proves the aggregate estimate. Persistence follows from the same latching argument and Lemma B.5. □\Box

Γv(Kv)​(δv)=Γv​(ρKv,δv)≤Γv​(Δveff2,δv)≤Λgap​Γv​(Δveff,δv).\Gamma_{v}^{(K_{v})}(\delta_{v})=\Gamma_{v}(\rho_{K_{v}},\delta_{v})\leq\Gamma_{v}\!\left(\frac{\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}}{2},\delta_{v}\right)\leq\Lambda_{\mathrm{gap}}\Gamma_{v}(\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}},\delta_{v}).

Otherwise, monotonicity makes the admissible set a prefix {0,…,Kx}\{0,\ldots,K_{x}\}, whose last cost satisfies Γv(Kx)​(δv)≤x\Gamma_{v}^{(K_{x})}(\delta_{v})\leq x. Applying prefix regularity once more,

We now compare the algorithm’s total spending with the recursive reference cost. This comparison must also account for the cap needed to make further progress: a child may be blocked even though that cap has not yet been spent. The next definition and lemma make this distinction precise.

Definition B.2 (Aggregate subtree call cost).

For a non-root node vv, let ℭv​(t)\mathfrak{C}_{v}(t) be the sum of the costs returned by all invocations at vv in the first tt completed outer-loop rounds. Equivalently, this is the slow cost at vv, together with all fast and slow costs strictly below vv; it excludes the fast query that first exposed vv. Set this quantity to zero for an unexposed node. Write Lvcost​(t)L_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(t) for the direct slow cost at vv, and Evcost​(t)E_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(t) for the remaining, recursive cost. Then

ℭv​(t)=Lvcost​(t)+Evcost​(t),Evcost​(t)=𝟏​{v​ expanded by ​t}​|Ch⁡(v)|+∑u∈Ch⁡(v)ℭu​(t).\mathfrak{C}_{v}(t)=L_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(t)+E_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(t),\qquad E_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(t)=\mathbf{1}\{v\text{ expanded by }t\}|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|+\sum_{u\in\mathrm{Ch}(v)}\mathfrak{C}_{u}(t).

The second term is zero at a leaf. Costs in a child subtree also appear in its ancestors’ costs, but no sum over all nodes is used: the root-child subtrees are disjoint, and their sum counts every post-initialization oracle cost exactly once.

Lemma B.15 (Minimum cap for an unresolved obligation).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}. At a fixed state of the algorithm, let (v,s,k)(v,s,k) be a finite unresolved obligation at an explored node, so that ¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t). There is a finite positive number dv​(s,k,t)d_{v}(s,k;t), called its minimum progress cap, such that Resolve​(v,s,k,B)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k,B) returns (0,𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽)(0,\mathsf{blocked}) exactly when B<dv​(s,k,t)B<d_{v}(s,k;t), and returns positive cost when B≥dv​(s,k,t)B\geq d_{v}(s,k;t). Fix the algorithm’s tie-breaking rules when defining this quantity. For an internal node set

R=αh⁡(v)​Γv(k)​(δv)−Mv,kexp​(t),bv=|Ch⁡(v)|.R=\alpha_{h(v)}\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v})-M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}(t),\qquad b_{v}=|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|.

The cap has the following recursive description:

  1. 1.

    If vv is a leaf, R≤0R\leq 0, or vv is unexpanded with bv>Rb_{v}>R, then dv​(s,k,t)=cd_{v}(s,k;t)=c.

  2. 2.

    If vv is unexpanded and bv≤Rb_{v}\leq R, then dv​(s,k,t)=bvd_{v}(s,k;t)=b_{v}.

  3. 3.

    Otherwise vv is expanded and R>0R>0. Let (u,su,ku)=ChildObligation​(v,s,k)(u,s_{u},k_{u})=\textsc{ChildObligation}(v,s,k), and write du=du​(su,ku,t)d_{u}=d_{u}(s_{u},k_{u};t). Then

    dv​(s,k,t)={du,du≤R,max⁡{R,c},du>R.d_{v}(s,k;t)=\begin{cases}d_{u},&d_{u}\leq R,\\ \max\{R,c\},&d_{u}>R.\end{cases}

In particular, at every internal node,

dv​(s,k,t)≤max⁡{R,c}.d_{v}(s,k;t)\leq\max\{R,c\}.

Moreover, if vv is expanded and Δveff≤2​ρk\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}\leq 2\rho_{k}, the child obligation selected by ChildObligation​(v,s,k)\textsc{ChildObligation}(v,s,k) satisfies Δueff≤2​ρku\Delta_{u}^{\mathrm{eff}}\leq 2\rho_{k_{u}}, regardless of the value of RR and whether the resolver actually reaches its child-call branch.

Proof. We prove the cap formula by induction on remaining depth. The local and expansion branches of Algorithm 4 give the first two cases directly. In the third case, Lemma B.4 supplies a finite unresolved child obligation. Certificate evaluations do not affect this argument: at fixed intervals, a bottom-up induction shows that latching a true certificate leaves all current completion predicates unchanged. Hence these zero-cost evaluations preserve both the selected obligation and its cap threshold.

If du≤Rd_{u}\leq R, the child receives enough cap exactly when B≥duB\geq d_{u}. If B<duB<d_{u}, then B<RB<R, so the parent passes the blocked return upward. If du>Rd_{u}>R, the child is blocked for every cap min⁡{B,R}\min\{B,R\}. The parent can then take a local step exactly when B≥RB\geq R and B≥cB\geq c. These are the two alternatives in the claimed formula. They also show that the threshold is finite and bounded by max⁡{R,c}\max\{R,c\}.

The child-selection rule and Lemma B.7 give ku≤kk_{u}\leq k and |V∗​(u)−V∗​(v)|≤ρku|V^{*}(u)-V^{*}(v)|\leq\rho_{k_{u}}. These bounds depend only on the current state and the child-selection rule; they do not require the child call to receive enough cap to perform work. Thus

Δueff=max⁡{Δveff,|V∗​(u)−V∗​(v)|}≤max⁡{2​ρk,ρku}≤2​ρku.\Delta_{u}^{\mathrm{eff}}=\max\{\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}},|V^{*}(u)-V^{*}(v)|\}\leq\max\{2\rho_{k},\rho_{k_{u}}\}\leq 2\rho_{k_{u}}.

□\Box

Proposition B.16 (Aggregate subtree charging).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}, ε=0\varepsilon=0, and Assumption 3.3, and let PhP_{h} be defined in Eq. (12). For every finite round TT and every non-root node vv,

ℭv​(T)≤Ph⁡(v)​Jv∗​(𝜹).\mathfrak{C}_{v}(T)\leq P_{h(v)}J_{v}^{*}(\boldsymbol{\delta}).

In fact, for every currently unresolved finite obligation (v,s,k)(v,s,k) with Δveff≤2​ρk\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}\leq 2\rho_{k}, the stronger bound holds:

ℭv​(T)+dv​(s,k,T)≤Ph⁡(v)​Jv∗​(𝜹).\mathfrak{C}_{v}(T)+d_{v}(s,k;T)\leq P_{h(v)}J_{v}^{*}(\boldsymbol{\delta}). (13)

Consequently,

CT≤|Ch⁡(r)|+PD−1​∑a∈Ch⁡(r)Ja∗​(𝜹)≤PD​H​(𝜹).C_{T}\leq|\mathrm{Ch}(r)|+P_{D-1}\sum_{a\in\mathrm{Ch}(r)}J_{a}^{*}(\boldsymbol{\delta})\leq P_{D}H(\boldsymbol{\delta}).

For αh=(h+1)2\alpha_{h}=(h+1)^{2},

PD≤Λloc​(1+αD)​∏i=1D(1+Λpreαi),P_{D}\leq\Lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}(1+\alpha_{D})\prod_{i=1}^{D}\left(1+\frac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{pre}}}{\alpha_{i}}\right),

so PD=OΛpre,Λgap​(D2)P_{D}=O_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{pre}},\Lambda_{\mathrm{gap}}}(D^{2}).

Proof. We use induction on remaining depth to prove the cost bound together with (13). The stronger claim is needed when a child call is blocked: past spending alone does not control the cap required for its next action. We prove both claims for every finite execution prefix and every current unresolved obligation satisfying the localization condition. Throughout, we consider states before new positive work and interpret undefined counters as zero. A blocked call changes neither intervals nor spending counters.

The local bound. We first bound spending by the cost of local certification. Each positive cost returned at scale jj increases exactly one of Mv,jlocM_{v,j}^{\mathrm{loc}} and Mv,jexpM_{v,j}^{\mathrm{exp}} by that cost. Proposition B.10 restricts every such scale to 𝒦vact\mathcal{K}_{v}^{\mathrm{act}}. Therefore Lemma B.13 gives

ℭv​(T)≤(1+αh⁡(v))​∑j∈𝒦vactΓv(j)​(δv).\mathfrak{C}_{v}(T)\leq(1+\alpha_{h(v)})\sum_{j\in\mathcal{K}_{v}^{\mathrm{act}}}\Gamma_{v}^{(j)}(\delta_{v}). (14)

To include the cap for a current unresolved obligation (v,s,k)(v,s,k), observe that k∈𝒦vactk\in\mathcal{K}_{v}^{\mathrm{act}}. Local scale completion then gives

Γv(k)​(δv)>0,Mv,kloc​(T)≤Γv(k)​(δv)−c.\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v})>0,\qquad M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{loc}}(T)\leq\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v})-c.

The subtraction is justified because both quantities are multiples of cc. For an internal node, write R=αh⁡(v)​Γv(k)−Mv,kexp≥0R=\alpha_{h(v)}\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}-M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}\geq 0. Lemma B.15 then gives

Mv,kloc+Mv,kexp+dv​(s,k,T)≤Mv,kloc+Mv,kexp+max⁡{R,c}≤(1+αh⁡(v))​Γv(k).\begin{split}M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{loc}}+M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}+d_{v}(s,k;T)&\leq M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{loc}}+M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}+\max\{R,c\}\\ &\leq(1+\alpha_{h(v)})\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}.\end{split}

The unused allowance at this scale therefore covers the additional cap: the right-hand side of (14) also bounds ℭv​(T)+dv​(s,k,T)\mathfrak{C}_{v}(T)+d_{v}(s,k;T). By Lemma B.14, both are at most (1+αh⁡(v))​Λloc​Γv​(Δveff,δv)(1+\alpha_{h(v)})\Lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}\Gamma_{v}(\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}},\delta_{v}). At a leaf, there is no recursive spending, so the bound reduces to Λloc​Γv​(Δveff,δv)\Lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}\Gamma_{v}(\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}},\delta_{v}). If an unresolved obligation exists, the unused local sample covers its cap cc. This proves the base case. It also proves both claims at an internal node whenever the local term attains the minimum defining Jv∗J_{v}^{*}.

The recursive bound. It remains to consider a node vv of remaining depth h≥1h\geq 1 for which the recursive term attains the minimum. Set

Qv≔Ph−1​(|Ch⁡(v)|+∑u∈Ch⁡(v)Ju∗​(𝜹))=Ph−1​Jv∗​(𝜹).Q_{v}\coloneqq P_{h-1}\left(|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|+\sum_{u\in\mathrm{Ch}(v)}J_{u}^{*}(\boldsymbol{\delta})\right)=P_{h-1}J_{v}^{*}(\boldsymbol{\delta}).

The cost induction hypothesis and Ph−1≥1P_{h-1}\geq 1 imply, at every earlier state t≤Tt\leq T,

Evcost​(t)≤Qv.E_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(t)\leq Q_{v}. (15)

Suppose vv is expanded and (v,s,k)(v,s,k) is a current unresolved obligation satisfying the localization condition. Let (u,su,ku)(u,s_{u},k_{u}) be the child obligation given by Lemma B.4. It exists even if the resolver has no recursive budget left, and it satisfies the localization condition by Lemma B.15. Apply the stronger induction hypothesis to this child and the ordinary cost bounds to all other children. This gives

Evcost​(t)+du​(su,ku,t)≤Qv.E_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(t)+d_{u}(s_{u},k_{u};t)\leq Q_{v}. (16)

This is the estimate that controls a blocked child call: it includes the cap needed for progress, even though that cap has not been spent.

We next bound the direct slow cost. We show that every scale kk at which a slow sample is issued at vv satisfies

αh​Γv(k)​(δv)<Qv.\alpha_{h}\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}(\delta_{v})<Q_{v}. (17)

Consider the state just before such a sample. By Proposition B.10, its obligation satisfies the localization condition. If vv is unexpanded, local sampling requires αh​Γv(k)<|Ch⁡(v)|≤Qv\alpha_{h}\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}<|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|\leq Q_{v}, since its recursive counter is still zero. If vv is expanded and its remaining budget RR is zero, then

αh​Γv(k)=Mv,kexp≤Evcost<Evcost+du≤Qv.\alpha_{h}\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}=M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}\leq E_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}<E_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}+d_{u}\leq Q_{v}.

If the node is expanded and R>0R>0, the resolver can fall back to local sampling only after a blocked child call, and only when its inherited cap is at least RR. The child therefore received cap RR, so Lemma B.15 gives du>Rd_{u}>R. Consequently,

αh​Γv(k)=Mv,kexp+R<Mv,kexp+du≤Evcost+du≤Qv.\alpha_{h}\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}=M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}+R<M_{v,k}^{\mathrm{exp}}+d_{u}\leq E_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}+d_{u}\leq Q_{v}.

Thus (17) holds whenever local sampling occurs. The local cost at each such scale is bounded by its local stopping cost. Summing these bounds with Lemma B.14 yields

Lvcost(T)≤∑{j:Γv(j)<Qv/αh}Γv(j)≤ΛpreαhQv.L_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(T)\leq\sum_{\{j:\,\Gamma_{v}^{(j)}<Q_{v}/\alpha_{h}\}}\Gamma_{v}^{(j)}\leq\frac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{pre}}}{\alpha_{h}}Q_{v}. (18)

Here the sum is taken over a finite prefix containing all scales used through TT. Together with (15), this proves the ordinary cost bound with factor (1+Λpre/αh)​Ph−1(1+\Lambda_{\mathrm{pre}}/\alpha_{h})P_{h-1}.

Including the cap for further progress. We must still include the current cap d=dv​(s,k,T)d=d_{v}(s,k;T). We show that it fits either the recursive bound or the unused local allowance. If vv is unexpanded and the expansion fits its recursive budget, then d=|Ch⁡(v)|d=|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|, Evcost=0E_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}=0, and Evcost+d≤QvE_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}+d\leq Q_{v}. If vv is expanded and its child’s cap fits the remaining budget, then d=dud=d_{u} and (16) gives the same conclusion. Finally, if du>R≥cd_{u}>R\geq c, then d=R<dud=R<d_{u}, so again Evcost+d≤QvE_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}+d\leq Q_{v}. In each case, the recursive bound covers the cap, and (18) covers the local spending.

In the remaining cases, d=cd=c and the next positive step is local sampling: either expansion exceeds the unexpanded node’s budget, R=0R=0, or du>Rd_{u}>R and R<cR<c. The argument for (17) applies to this scale as well, even if no sample has yet been issued there. Moreover, Mv,kloc≤Γv(k)−cM_{v,k}^{\mathrm{loc}}\leq\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}-c, since the current obligation is unresolved. One additional local sample therefore leaves the direct local cost at this scale at most Γv(k)\Gamma_{v}^{(k)}. Applying the threshold sum to the previously sampled scales and the current scale gives

Lvcost​(T)+d≤Λpreαh​Qv.L_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(T)+d\leq\frac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{pre}}}{\alpha_{h}}Q_{v}.

Together with Evcost​(T)≤QvE_{v}^{\mathrm{cost}}(T)\leq Q_{v}, this proves in every case

ℭv​(T)+dv​(s,k,T)≤(1+Λpreαh)​Qv≤Ph​Jv∗​(𝜹).\mathfrak{C}_{v}(T)+d_{v}(s,k;T)\leq\left(1+\frac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{pre}}}{\alpha_{h}}\right)Q_{v}\leq P_{h}J_{v}^{*}(\boldsymbol{\delta}).

This completes the simultaneous induction.

Summing at the root. The root’s only direct cost is the initialization cost |Ch⁡(r)||\mathrm{Ch}(r)|, and every subsequent cost belongs to exactly one root-child subtree. Since Ph≥Ph−1≥1P_{h}\geq P_{h-1}\geq 1 follows directly from Eq. (12), the claimed root bounds follow. Finally, unrolling that recursion and using the nondecreasing sequence αh\alpha_{h} gives the stated product bound. For αh=(h+1)2\alpha_{h}=(h+1)^{2}, its product is at most

exp⁡(Λpre​∑i=1∞1(i+1)2),\exp\!\left(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pre}}\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(i+1)^{2}}\right),

while its remaining factor is O⁡(D2)O(D^{2}). □\Box

Lemma B.17 (Positive progress of unresolved selected calls).

Let

qmin≔min⁡{c,1}>0.q_{\min}\coloneqq\min\{c,1\}>0.

Consider any invocation Resolve​(v,s,k,B)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k,B) with finite scale kk that begins at a round tt with

¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t).\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t).

Then the invocation either returns (0,𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽)(0,\mathsf{blocked}), or returns a pair (q,z)(q,z) with q≥qminq\geq q_{\min}. In particular, if B=+∞B=+\infty, then the invocation returns cost at least qminq_{\min}.

Proof. We argue by induction on the remaining depth h⁡(v)h(v). At a leaf, h⁡(v)=0h(v)=0, the first guard in Resolve​(v,s,k,B)\textsc{Resolve}(v,s,k,B) is false because the obligation is unresolved. The procedure therefore calls LocalStep​(v,k,B)\textsc{LocalStep}(v,k,B), which returns (0,𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽)(0,\mathsf{blocked}) if B<cB<c, and otherwise takes one slow sample at cost c≥qminc\geq q_{\min}.

Suppose h⁡(v)≥1h(v)\geq 1 and the claim holds for the children of vv. The first guard is again false. A nonpositive remaining recursive budget leads directly to LocalStep​(v,k,B)\textsc{LocalStep}(v,k,B), whose behavior was just established. If vv is unexpanded and |Ch⁡(v)|>R|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|>R, the same fallback LocalStep​(v,k,B)\textsc{LocalStep}(v,k,B) applies. For an unexpanded node in the remaining case, |Ch⁡(v)|≤R|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|\leq R: the expansion is affordable from the node’s own budget. If |Ch⁡(v)|>B|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|>B, the inherited cap blocks it and the invocation returns (0,𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽)(0,\mathsf{blocked}). If this cap also permits the expansion, the procedure expands vv at cost |Ch⁡(v)|≥1≥qmin|\mathrm{Ch}(v)|\geq 1\geq q_{\min}.

Only the expanded-node case with positive recursive budget requires the induction hypothesis. Lemma B.4 ensures that 𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(v,k,t)\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(v,k,t) being false provides a finite capped child obligation. In a selector case, the chosen child (u,s,ku)(u,s,k_{u}) satisfies

ku=Ks≤k​(u,t)<+∞and¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(u,ku,t).k_{u}=K_{s}^{\leq k}(u,t)<+\infty\qquad\text{and}\qquad\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(u,k_{u},t).

In a comparison case, the blocker is called on the opposite side s¯\bar{s} when a finite capped obligation remains there, and otherwise on side ss. The definition of K⋅≤kK_{\cdot}^{\leq k} ensures that either call targets an unresolved obligation, so the induction hypothesis applies. A positive child cost is returned unchanged. After a child return of (0,𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽)(0,\mathsf{blocked}), the parent either also returns (0,𝖻𝗅𝗈𝖼𝗄𝖾𝖽)(0,\mathsf{blocked}) because the inherited cap is binding, or calls LocalStep​(v,k,B)\textsc{LocalStep}(v,k,B). That local step is itself blocked or costs at least qminq_{\min}, completing the induction.

When B=+∞B=+\infty, the inherited cap cannot block progress and LocalStep​(v,k,B)\textsc{LocalStep}(v,k,B) is always affordable. The invocation therefore returns cost at least qminq_{\min}. □\Box

Lemma B.18 (Non-stopping rounds select a finite unresolved side).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta} and ε=0\varepsilon=0. In every outer-loop round before stopping, Algorithm 1 selects a root child xx, side ss, and scale k<+∞k<+\infty such that

¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉s​(x,k,t).\neg\mathsf{Comp}_{s}(x,k,t).

Proof. Let aa and bb be the current leader and challenger, with respective scales ka=KL​(a,t)k_{a}=K_{L}(a,t) and kb=K±​(b,t)k_{b}=K_{\pm}(b,t). The selection rule prefers a finite scale: if ka<+∞k_{a}<+\infty and kb=+∞k_{b}=+\infty, it selects the leader at scale kak_{a}; if ka=+∞k_{a}=+\infty and kb<+∞k_{b}<+\infty, it selects the challenger at scale kbk_{b}; and if both scales are finite, it selects the coarser one. Thus an infinite selected scale would require

KL​(a,t)=+∞andK±​(b,t)=+∞.K_{L}(a,t)=+\infty\qquad\text{and}\qquad K_{\pm}(b,t)=+\infty.

By the definition of K±K_{\pm}, the second equality means

KL​(b,t)=KU​(b,t)=+∞.K_{L}(b,t)=K_{U}(b,t)=+\infty.

These equalities are incompatible with a failed stopping test. Indeed, if KL​(a,t)=+∞K_{L}(a,t)=+\infty, Lemma B.8 gives

V∗​(r,a)−La​(t)=0.V^{*}(r,a)-L_{a}(t)=0.

Likewise, KL​(b,t)=KU​(b,t)=+∞K_{L}(b,t)=K_{U}(b,t)=+\infty gives

V∗​(r,b)−Lb​(t)=0,Ub​(t)−V∗​(r,b)=0.V^{*}(r,b)-L_{b}(t)=0,\qquad U_{b}(t)-V^{*}(r,b)=0.

Failure of the stopping test means

La​(t)<Ub​(t).L_{a}(t)<U_{b}(t).

Together, these relations imply V∗​(r,a)<V∗​(r,b)V^{*}(r,a)<V^{*}(r,b), and hence

Lb​(t)=V∗​(r,b)>V∗​(r,a)=La​(t),L_{b}(t)=V^{*}(r,b)>V^{*}(r,a)=L_{a}(t),

contradicting the choice of aa as a leader with maximal lower endpoint. The selected scale must therefore be finite. By the definitions of KLK_{L}, KUK_{U}, and K±K_{\pm}, every finite selected scale is unresolved, giving the required ¬𝖢𝗈𝗆𝗉\neg\mathsf{Comp} condition. □\Box

Proposition B.19 (Finite stopping and correctness).

Assume ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}, ε=0\varepsilon=0, and Assumption 3.3. Then Algorithm 1 halts after finitely many oracle calls. At its stopping time τ\tau, every returned action a^τ\hat{a}_{\tau} is the unique optimal root action a∗a^{*}.

Proof. We combine the uniform bound on finite execution prefixes with a positive cost in every non-stopping round. Consistency of the confidence radii gives Γv​(Δveff,δv)<∞\Gamma_{v}(\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}},\delta_{v})<\infty at every non-root node vv, since Δveff≥Δ∗>0\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}\geq\Delta_{*}>0. It follows that Jv∗​(𝜹)<∞J_{v}^{*}(\boldsymbol{\delta})<\infty for every non-root vv, by induction on h⁡(v)h(v), and the tree’s finiteness then gives H⁡(𝜹)<∞H(\boldsymbol{\delta})<\infty. Proposition B.16 bounds every finite prefix:

CT≤PD​H​(𝜹)for every finite round ​T.C_{T}\leq P_{D}H(\boldsymbol{\delta})\qquad\text{for every finite round }T.

Suppose the algorithm never stops. In each outer-loop round, Lemma B.18 supplies a finite unresolved call Resolve​(x,s,k,+∞)\textsc{Resolve}(x,s,k,+\infty). The finite scale searches and finite recursion depth ensure that each round completes. By Lemma B.17, its cost is at least qmin>0q_{\min}>0. After NN non-stopping rounds, the total cost is therefore at least the initialization cost plus N​qminNq_{\min}. This diverges as N→∞N\to\infty, contradicting the uniform bound PD​H​(𝜹)P_{D}H(\boldsymbol{\delta}). The algorithm must halt after finitely many oracle calls.

At the stopping time τ\tau, the returned action a^τ\hat{a}_{\tau} satisfies

La^τ​(τ)≥maxa≠a^τ⁡Ua​(τ).L_{\hat{a}_{\tau}}(\tau)\geq\max_{a\neq\hat{a}_{\tau}}U_{a}(\tau).

Lemma 2.4 makes every root-child interval valid on ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}, so

V∗​(r,a^τ)≥La^τ​(τ)≥maxa≠a^τ⁡Ua​(τ)≥maxa≠a^τ⁡V∗​(r,a).V^{*}(r,\hat{a}_{\tau})\geq L_{\hat{a}_{\tau}}(\tau)\geq\max_{a\neq\hat{a}_{\tau}}U_{a}(\tau)\geq\max_{a\neq\hat{a}_{\tau}}V^{*}(r,a).

Thus a^τ\hat{a}_{\tau} is optimal, and uniqueness gives a^τ=a∗\hat{a}_{\tau}=a^{*}. □\Box

B.6 Proof of Theorem 3.6

We now assemble the bounds established in Appendix B.5.

Proof. When ρ0=0\rho_{0}=0, initialization already determines the answer, as shown at the start of Appendix B.5. The cost bound follows from Cτ=H⁡(𝜹)C_{\tau}=H(\boldsymbol{\delta}) and PD≥1P_{D}\geq 1. Assume ρ0>0\rho_{0}>0 below. On ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}, finite stopping and correctness follow from Proposition B.19. Now that τ\tau is known to be finite, Proposition B.16 applies with T=τT=\tau and gives

Cτ≤PD​H​(𝜹).C_{\tau}\leq P_{D}H(\boldsymbol{\delta}).

The 𝒪⁡(D2)\mathcal{O}(D^{2}) form follows from the final statement of Proposition B.16 for αh=(h+1)2\alpha_{h}=(h+1)^{2}.

By Eq. (5), each feasible allocation satisfies ℙ⁡(ℰδ)≥1−δ\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_{\delta})\geq 1-\delta. For the optimized statement, choose a near-optimal feasible allocation 𝜹η\boldsymbol{\delta}^{\eta} satisfying the uniform regularity condition in Theorem 3.6, with

H⁡(𝜹η)≤H∗+η.H(\boldsymbol{\delta}^{\eta})\leq H^{*}+\eta.

Apply the fixed-allocation bound to the run using this allocation, on its corresponding simultaneous-validity event. This gives the claimed high-probability optimized bound. If an allocation attaining the infimum satisfies the same regularity constants, take η=0\eta=0. Otherwise, H∗≥|Ch⁡(r)|≥2H^{*}\geq|\mathrm{Ch}(r)|\geq 2 ensures that any η≤H∗\eta\leq H^{*} gives the stated H∗H^{*}-order bound. □\Box

B.7 Proofs and Qualifications for Oracle Robustness

The robustness results control the probability of an incorrect finite output. Extending the unbiased finite-stopping or cost theorem would require additional assumptions.

B.7.1 Proof of Theorem 3.7

Write θv=V∗​(v)+bv\theta_{v}=V^{*}(v)+b_{v}. To account for the bias, replace Eq. (4) by

IvS,ξ​(t)=⋂j=1NvS​(t)[V^v,j−βv​(j,δv)−ξ,V^v,j+βv​(j,δv)+ξ],I_{v}^{S,\xi}(t)=\bigcap_{j=1}^{N_{v}^{S}(t)}[\widehat{V}_{v,j}-\beta_{v}(j,\delta_{v})-\xi,\widehat{V}_{v,j}+\beta_{v}(j,\delta_{v})+\xi],

where the intersection is (−∞,+∞)(-\infty,+\infty) before any samples are taken. The fast intervals, minimax backups, and root stopping test are unchanged. The assumed concentration around the biased mean is

ℙ(∃n≥1:|V^v,n−θv|>βv(n,δv))≤δv.\mathbb{P}\!\left(\exists n\geq 1:|\widehat{V}_{v,n}-\theta_{v}|>\beta_{v}(n,\delta_{v})\right)\leq\delta_{v}.

Proof. A union bound gives an event of probability at least 1−δ1-\delta on which, simultaneously for all nodes and sample counts, |V^v,n−θv|≤βv​(n,δv)|\widehat{V}_{v,n}-\theta_{v}|\leq\beta_{v}(n,\delta_{v}). On this event,

|V^v,n−V∗​(v)|≤βv​(n,δv)+ξ.|\widehat{V}_{v,n}-V^{*}(v)|\leq\beta_{v}(n,\delta_{v})+\xi.

Every inflated slow interval therefore contains the true node value, as does every fast interval. Their intersections remain nonempty and valid, and induction through the max and min backups preserves validity without further inflation. The inconsistency exit consequently cannot occur on this event. The root stopping argument from Theorem 3.1 now proves the claim. □\Box

Why interval inflation is required.

Without inflation, the endpoint inequalities Lv≤V∗​(v)+ξL_{v}\leq V^{*}(v)+\xi and Uv≥V∗​(v)−ξU_{v}\geq V^{*}(v)-\xi would bound the error by ε+2​ξ\varepsilon+2\xi whenever the root stopping test returns a separated recommendation. But they do not ensure Lv≤UvL_{v}\leq U_{v}: a fast interval containing V∗​(v)V^{*}(v) may be disjoint from a narrow slow interval around V∗​(v)+bvV^{*}(v)+b_{v}. They therefore cannot, by themselves, guarantee correctness of the unmodified algorithm for arbitrary biased oracles. Inflation by the known bias bound preserves valid, nonempty intervals. The inflated radius need not tend to zero, however, so the unbiased finite-stopping and cost proofs do not carry over.

B.7.2 Proof of Theorem 3.8

Proof. The enlarged fast interval contains V∗​(v)V^{*}(v). On ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}, every slow interval also contains V∗​(v)V^{*}(v), so local intersections and minimax backups remain valid. The stopping-rule proof applies, and the inconsistency exit cannot occur on ℰδ\mathcal{E}_{\delta}.

For the fixed-history comparison, intersecting a larger fast interval with the same slow interval gives a larger local interval. Enlarging the child intervals weakly decreases their lower endpoints and weakly increases their upper endpoints; both max and min backups preserve these inequalities. Induction up the common exposed tree, with the enlarged local intervals intersected at each node, proves the claimed containment. Actual adaptive runs may choose different queries and expansions, so this comparison does not order their realized costs. □\Box

B.8 Qualifications for the Reference Complexity and Local Regularity

The correctness theorem bounds the unconditional probability that the algorithm stops and returns a recommendation that violates the requested accuracy.

We also note that the half-gap condition in Assumption 3.3 restricts how the hybrid cost curve may cross the deterministic fast-bias cutoff. If

Δveff/8<B⁡(h⁡(v))≤Δveff/4,\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}/8<B(h(v))\leq\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}/4,

then Γv​(Δveff,δv)=0\Gamma_{v}(\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}},\delta_{v})=0 but Γv​(Δveff/2,δv)>0\Gamma_{v}(\Delta_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}/2,\delta_{v})>0, so the condition fails. Polynomial scaling of the slow-sample cost alone therefore does not establish regularity of the hybrid curve.
